title: dedicated-autoscaler-slo-tuning-and-burst-util-reporting-fix
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: several customers running Dedicated fleets observed spurious utilization alerts and degraded throughput during short-lived burst traffic. This PR fixes two related issues: 1) the autoscaler token-bucket smoothing math could under-report effective available burst capacity when multi-priority queues were active, leading to unnecessary scale-ups; 2) the utilization reporter emitted transient 100% utilization spikes when queue draining coincided with burst smoothing resets. Changes: - Adjust token-bucket smoothing constants and introduce a small hysteresis window to prevent flip-flop scale decisions under rapid burst arrivals. - Correct priority-weighted capacity accounting so higher-priority reservations do not zero-out shared capacity when idle tasks are present. - Add a rolling-window percentile (95th) to the utilization reporter and ignore sub-100ms sample outliers to reduce false positive alerts. - Expose two new config flags (autoscaler.smoothing_hysteresis_ms, reporting.ignore_short_samples_ms) with sensible defaults to allow gradual rollout. - Add unit + integration tests and updated telemetry to validate behavior under synthetic burst traces. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-3421) - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Integration test harness run with representative traces - [x] Telemetry and dashboards updated - [x] Docs note for Dedicated SLO tuning (console) Related: ENG-3499 (incident follow-up), internal runbook updated at docs/runbooks/dedicated-autoscaler.md

review_comments: Liam Chen: Can you justify the chosen hysteresis default? Requesting a short rationale in the config comment so operators understand trade-offs.
Aisha Patel: Default chosen after running 100 synthetic bursts; 200ms showed stable behavior across instance sizes. Added comment and linked benchmark results.
Marina Gomez: Please add a regression test that simulates priority inversion with idle high-priority reservations.
Aisha Patel: Added a deterministic integration test that reproduces the scenario and verifies no scale-up is triggered.
Omar Hassan: CI flake on integration tests initially; re-ran and added small retry in harness to avoid false negatives.
Marina Gomez: Approve after minor nit fixes.
release_notes: Fixed Dedicated autoscaler and utilization reporting: reduced false-positive utilization alerts during short bursts, improved priority-weighted capacity accounting, and added configurable hysteresis to autoscaler smoothing. Recommended for Dedicated fleets experiencing spurious scale-ups.
notes_for_ops: Rollout plan: 1) Deploy with defaults to 10% of fleets using canary tag, 2) Monitor autoscaler_smoothing_events_total and utilization_95th_ms for 48h, 3) If steady, increase to 50% then full rollout. If regressions, revert flag autoscaler.smoothing_hysteresis_ms to previous value.
notes: This is a targeted change focused on Dedicated fleets and should not affect hosted API defaults. Config flags allow customers to opt into more aggressive or relaxed hysteresis via the console.
